[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"NumPy Tutorial: Arrays and Linear Algebra in Python"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"NumPy (Numerical Python) is a fundamental package for scientific computing in Python. It provides support for large, multi-dimensional arrays and matrices, along with a collection of mathematical functions to operate on these arrays efficiently. This tutorial covers the basics of NumPy arrays and introduces linear algebra operations."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"NumPy Arrays"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A NumPy array is a grid of values, all of the same type, and is indexed by a tuple of non-negative integers. The number of dimensions is the rank of the array; the shape of an array is a tuple of integers giving the size of the array along each dimension."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating NumPy Arrays"},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"# Import the NumPy library
import numpy as np

# Create a 1D array from a list
arr1 = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
print("1D Array:", arr1)

# Create a 2D array from a list of lists
arr2 = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
print("2D Array:\n", arr2)

# Create an array of zeros
arr_zeros = np.zeros((2, 3))
print("Array of Zeros:\n", arr_zeros)

# Create an array of ones
arr_ones = np.ones((3, 2))
print("Array of Ones:\n", arr_ones)

# Create an array of a specific value
arr_full = np.full((2, 2), 7)
print("Full Array:\n", arr_full)

# Create an identity matrix
arr_eye = np.eye(3)
print("Identity Matrix:\n", arr_eye)

# Create an array with a range of values
arr_range = np.arange(0, 20, 2) # Start, stop, step
print("Range Array:", arr_range)

# Create an array with evenly spaced values within a range
arr_linspace = np.linspace(0, 1, 5) # Start, stop, number of values
print("Linspace Array:", arr_linspace)"},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Array Indexing and Slicing"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"NumPy offers several ways to index into arrays. Slicing is similar to Python list slicing."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"# Indexing
print("Element at index 0 of arr1:", arr1[0])
print("Element at row 0, column 1 of arr2:", arr2[0, 1])

# Slicing
print("First 3 elements of arr1:", arr1[0:3])
print("First row of arr2:", arr2[0, :])
print("First column of arr2:", arr2[:, 0])"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Array Math"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Basic mathematical functions operate elementwise on arrays, and are available both as operator overloads and as functions in the NumPy module."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"# Elementwise addition
arr_add = arr1 + 2
print("Addition:", arr_add)

# Elementwise subtraction
arr_sub = arr1 - 1
print("Subtraction:", arr_sub)

# Elementwise multiplication
arr_mul = arr1 * 3
print("Multiplication:", arr_mul)

# Elementwise division
arr_div = arr1 / 2
print("Division:", arr_div)

# Elementwise square root
arr_sqrt = np.sqrt(arr1)
print("Square Root:", arr_sqrt)

# Sum of all elements
arr_sum = np.sum(arr1)
print("Sum:", arr_sum)

# Mean of all elements
arr_mean = np.mean(arr1)
print("Mean:", arr_mean)"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Linear Algebra"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"NumPy provides functions for performing linear algebra operations, such as matrix multiplication, finding determinants, and solving linear systems."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"# Matrix multiplication
matrix1 = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
matrix2 = np.array([[5, 6], [7, 8]])
matrix_product = np.dot(matrix1, matrix2)
print("Matrix Product:\n", matrix_product)

# Transpose of a matrix
matrix_transpose = np.transpose(matrix1)
print("Matrix Transpose:\n", matrix_transpose)

# Determinant of a matrix
matrix_det = np.linalg.det(matrix1)
print("Matrix Determinant:", matrix_det)

# Inverse of a matrix
try:
    matrix_inv = np.linalg.inv(matrix1)
    print("Matrix Inverse:\n", matrix_inv)
except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
    print("Matrix is singular and has no inverse.")

# Solving a linear system (Ax = b)
A = np.array([[2, 1], [1, 3]])
b = np.array([1, 2])
x = np.linalg.solve(A, b)
print("Solution to linear system:", x)"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Broadcasting"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Broadcasting is a powerful mechanism that allows NumPy to work with arrays of different shapes when performing arithmetic operations. Smaller arrays are "broadcast" across the larger array so that they have compatible shapes."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"# Example of broadcasting
arr = np.array([1, 2, 3])
scalar = 5

# The scalar is broadcast to match the shape of the array
result = arr + scalar
print("Broadcasting Result:", result)"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Reshaping Arrays"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"The shape of an array can be changed without changing its data."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"# Reshape an array
arr = np.arange(12)
reshaped_arr = arr.reshape(3, 4)
print("Original Array:", arr)
print("Reshaped Array:\n", reshaped_arr)"},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a basic introduction to NumPy arrays and linear algebra operations. NumPy is a powerful tool for numerical computing in Python, and mastering it is essential for data science, machine learning, and scientific computing."}]
